From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Jared Thompson <jared.thompson@acme.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@acme.com>
Cc: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Acme - SDK auth & RSP schema follow-up

Thanks Jared — good questions. High-level answers here; we can dive deeper on the engineer call.

1) Chat vs Completions + structured output/tool-calling
- Recommendation: use our chat endpoint with function/tool-calling for the invoicing assistant. Chat provides richer turn-level metadata (role, name, tool results) and is optimized in our runtime for low-latency incremental generation. For strict JSON output, use a shallow schema (single top-level object) and the SDK will enforce validation/structured output to reduce hallucinations.

2) Tokenization & max_tokens
- Tokenization: we use a BPE-ish tokenizer; the safe rule is plan for ~1.3–1.6 chars per token for English. For 700 chars expect ~430–540 tokens worst-case depending on punctuation and whitespace.
- max_tokens: set your response budget conservatively (e.g., 256–512) for assistant replies when you have long context histories to avoid hitting the model window. Our SDK exposes token_estimate utilities to compute prompt+resp before send.

3) Streaming semantics & token accounting
- Streaming: our chat streaming sends tokens as they are generated over a single SSE/HTTP2 stream. The SDK takes care of reassembling partial tokens and emitting events.
- Accounting: token usage is measured on the server once generation completes or when the stream is terminated; partial streaming chunks do not finalize billing until the response is ended/aborted. If you cancel mid-stream, you are billed for tokens generated up to cancel. We can also configure soft timeouts to cap long-running generations.

4) Embeddings + reranker pattern
- Typical pattern: 1) embed query + documents, 2) retrieve top-K (vector similarity), 3) run a reranker (lightweight model or scoring pass) or a model-based re-ranking/answer generation. For latency-sensitive use cases, run a small neural reranker (cheap) and only escalate to full model scoring for top candidates. Redwood supports both flows; we can show latency/cost tradeoffs with your data.

5) Auth for Private deployment
- SAML SSO + IdP integration: supported via our Private control plane. We integrate with SAML providers and can map groups/roles. For on-prem, we can deploy a small auth connector that proxies SAML assertions to the control plane. KMS integrations for key management are supported (bring-your-own-key). I'll attach an auth flow diagram.

Next steps:
- I'm proposing a 45m technical deep-dive Thu 11/19 10:30–11:15 PT with Michael (infra/runtime) and Dylan (SDK/infra). Confirmable?
- We'll share the RSP schema examples and a short SDK snippet showing auth + streaming usage (attached).

Attachments: redwood_sdk_auth_flow.png, rsp_schema_examples.md

Best,
Marissa

- Reranker: we have a small transformer-based reranker that runs ~30–70ms per doc on our infra; costs ~10–15% of a full generation pass when used as a scorer. We'll include sample numbers for K=10.
- Private SAML: supported, but depending on their IdP we may need to add an auth connector. No blocker but needs network config.

I'll add a short deck with numbers to the call notes pre-meeting.
